interactions.label: According to the video, what did the WHO Director-General declare on 30 January

params.question: According to the video, what did the WHO Director-General declare on 30 January 2020, in response to the Wuhan pneumonia cluster?

answers.text: A pandemic

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not quite — WHO upgraded to a pandemic declaration only later, on 11 March 2020, after further global spread.

answers.text: A Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This was only the sixth PHEIC declared under the IHR 2005 framework, made by the Director-General on the advice of an Emergency Committee.

answers.text: A Grade 3 Emergency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: WHO's internal emergency grading system is a separate operational classification used for resource mobilisation, not the formal declaration described here.

answers.text: A Global Outbreak Alert

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GOARN coordinates operational outbreak response, but the formal legal declaration made on 30 January 2020 was a PHEIC.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the timeline: PHEIC was declared 30 January 2020; the pandemic declaration followed 40 days later, on 11 March 2020.
Right — the PHEIC is the formal trigger under IHR 2005 that mobilises coordinated international action.

interactions.label: Which statement best explains why international cooperation is considered essent

params.question: Which statement best explains why international cooperation is considered essential in public health?

answers.text: Pathogens do not respect political borders, so disease control requires countries to act together

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is the basic epidemiological reasoning behind international health — diseases, vectors, and even trade in food and medicines cross borders regardless of national policy.

answers.text: All countries carry an equal share of the global disease burden, so pooling resources is simply efficient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not accurate — the video states low- and middle-income countries carry about 80% of the global communicable disease burden while holding under 20% of global health resources. The burden is highly unequal, not equal.

answers.text: Cooperation is mainly needed to standardise vaccination schedules across countries

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vaccine schedule harmonisation is only one narrow activity; the broader rationale is shared vulnerability to cross-border spread of disease and other health threats.

answers.text: Only high-income countries face significant communicable disease threats

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is the opposite of what the video describes — the greatest communicable disease burden falls on low- and middle-income countries.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall Park's triad from the video: international health deals with problems that cross borders because people, products, and disease vectors move between countries.
Exactly — shared vulnerability, not shared resources, is what drives multilateral health cooperation.

interactions.label: Which agency is the directing and coordinating authority on international health

params.question: Which agency is the directing and coordinating authority on international health within the UN system, headquartered in Geneva and governed by the World Health Assembly?

answers.text: UNICEF

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: UNICEF, headquartered in New York, focuses on child and maternal health, nutrition, and immunisation — it does not hold WHO's normative authority.

answers.text: UNFPA

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: UNFPA addresses reproductive health and family planning from its New York headquarters, not the overall directing role in international health.

answers.text: World Health Organization (WHO)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO, established in 1948 and headquartered in Geneva, is the directing and coordinating authority on international health, governed annually by the World Health Assembly of 194 member states.

answers.text: World Bank

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The World Bank, based in Washington DC, is the largest single financier of LMIC health programmes, but it is not the WHA-governed normative authority.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the four tiers: WHO is the UN-affiliated body governed by the World Health Assembly and headquartered in Geneva.
Correct — WHO sits at the apex of the first tier, setting global norms and running the IHR 2005 framework.

interactions.label: Which of the following best explains why IHR 2005 is considered more comprehensi

params.question: Which of the following best explains why IHR 2005 is considered more comprehensive than the older International Sanitary Regulations it replaced?

answers.text: It expanded coverage from three named diseases (cholera, plague, yellow fever) to any event that could become a Public Health Emergency of International Concern

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This broadened scope is what allows IHR 2005 to apply to novel threats like SARS-CoV-2, which were not on the old fixed disease list.

answers.text: It reduced the number of countries legally bound by the regulations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The opposite is true — IHR 2005 binds 196 states parties, more than WHO's own 194 member states.

answers.text: It removed the obligation for countries to notify WHO of outbreaks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IHR 2005 actually strengthens notification obligations — countries, including India, must notify WHO within 24 hours of suspecting a PHEIC.

answers.text: It restricted its scope exclusively to vaccine-preventable diseases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IHR 2005 is broader, not narrower — it covers any serious, internationally-relevant public health event, not just vaccine-preventable ones.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: IHR 2005 moved away from naming specific diseases and instead covers any event that could become a PHEIC.
Right — moving from a fixed disease list to an all-hazards PHEIC trigger is the key reform of IHR 2005.

interactions.label: How does WHO's accountability mechanism differ structurally from that of a bilat

params.question: How does WHO's accountability mechanism differ structurally from that of a bilateral agency such as USAID?

answers.text: WHO is accountable to the World Health Assembly and Joint Inspection Unit against GPW13 targets, while bilateral agencies are held accountable through evaluations commissioned by their own boards and donors, often tied to verified results

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO's multilateral, member-state-governed accountability contrasts with the donor/board-driven, results-tied accountability of bilateral agencies like USAID or JICA.

answers.text: Both are accountable solely to the UN Security Council

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Neither WHO nor bilateral agencies report to the Security Council — WHO answers to the WHA, and bilateral agencies answer to their own governments and donors.

answers.text: Bilateral agencies report to WHO's Director-General, while WHO itself has no oversight body

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This reverses the relationship — WHO has robust oversight through the WHA and JIU, while bilateral agencies operate independently under their own donor governments.

answers.text: WHO has no formal accountability mechanism, unlike bilateral agencies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: WHO is in fact tracked closely through budget reviews, DG reports, JIU evaluations, and progress against GPW13's triple billion targets.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the video's contrast: WHO answers to the WHA and JIU against GPW13 targets, while bilateral agencies are evaluated by their own boards and donors.
Exactly — multilateral member-state governance versus donor/board-driven evaluation is the key structural difference.

interactions.label: A district health officer suspects an outbreak of international concern. Per the

params.question: A district health officer suspects an outbreak of international concern. Per the reporting chain described in the video, which body receives the report after it passes through the state level, before it reaches the Directorate General of Health Services and WHO?

answers.text: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NCDC is India's designated national focal point under IHR 2005 and sits between the state level and the DGHS/WHO in the reporting chain.

answers.text: Serum Institute of India

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Serum Institute is a vaccine manufacturer, not part of the disease surveillance reporting chain.

answers.text: GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: GAVI is a public-private partnership that funds vaccine access; it plays no role in India's outbreak reporting chain.

answers.text: WHO's SEARO office directly, bypassing national authorities

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Reports do not skip national authorities — they move from district to state to NCDC to DGHS before reaching WHO's regional and global offices.

overallFeedback.feedback: Retrace the chain: district surveillance unit → state → NCDC → DGHS → WHO regional/global offices.
Correct — NCDC is the critical national node linking domestic surveillance (IDSP) to WHO's international framework.
